/-!
# Erdős Problem 594

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/594](https://www.erdosproblems.com/594)
- [ErHa66] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A., On chromatic number of graphs and set-systems.
  Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1966), 61-99.
- [Er69b] Erdős, P., Problems and results in chromatic graph theory. Proof Techniques in
  Graph Theory (Proc. Second Ann Arbor Graph Theory Conf., Ann Arbor, Mich., 1968)
  (1969), 27-35.
- [EHS74] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A. and Shelah, S., On some general properties of chromatic
  numbers. Topics in topology (Proc. Colloq., Keszthely, 1972) (1974), 243-255.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Cardinal
open scoped Cardinal

namespace Erdos594

/--
**Erdős Problem 594** (Erdős–Hajnal [ErHa66], [Er69b]):

Does every graph $G$ with chromatic number $\geq \aleph_1$ contain all sufficiently
large odd cycles?

The answer is **Yes**, proved by Erdős, Hajnal, and Shelah [EHS74].

A graph has chromatic number $\geq \aleph_1$ (i.e. uncountable chromatic number)
if and only if it admits no proper colouring with countably many colours; this is
encoded as `IsEmpty (G.Coloring ℕ)`. The conclusion states that there is some
$N$ such that for every $k \geq N$ the graph contains a cycle of odd length $2k + 1$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 3 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1268917deaaaa0d674f651287027baa26cea9920/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos594.lean#L907"]
theorem erdos_594 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), IsEmpty (G.Coloring ℕ) →
      ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ k : ℕ, N ≤ k →
        ∃ (v : V) (w : G.Walk v v), w.IsCycle ∧ w.length = 2 * k + 1 := by
  sorry

/--
The earlier result of Erdős and Hajnal [ErHa66]: every graph with chromatic number
$\geq \aleph_2$ contains all sufficiently large odd cycles.

Chromatic number $\geq \aleph_2$ is encoded as the nonexistence of a proper colouring
with any set of at most $\aleph_1$ colours.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 3 5]
theorem erdos_594.variants.erdos_hajnal (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V)
    (h : ∀ (α : Type), #α ≤ ℵ_ 1 → IsEmpty (G.Coloring α)) :
    ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ k : ℕ, N ≤ k →
      ∃ (v : V) (w : G.Walk v v), w.IsCycle ∧ w.length = 2 * k + 1 := by
  sorry

/--
Sanity check for the encoding of "chromatic number $\geq \aleph_1$": a countably
colourable graph, such as the empty graph on $\mathbb{N}$, does not satisfy the
hypothesis `IsEmpty (G.Coloring ℕ)`.
-/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_594.variants.bot_countably_colorable :
    ¬ IsEmpty ((⊥ : SimpleGraph ℕ).Coloring ℕ) := by
  rw [not_isEmpty_iff]
  exact ⟨SimpleGraph.Coloring.mk (fun _ => 0) (by simp)⟩

end Erdos594

reformulations.difference: Uses the absence of an ℕ-valued proper colouring for uncountable chromatic number, and closed IsCycle walks of length 2*k+1 for containment of sufficiently large odd cycles.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A graph admits an ℕ-valued proper colouring exactly when its chromatic cardinal is at most ℵ₀, so IsEmpty (G.Coloring ℕ) is equivalent to χ(G) ≥ ℵ₁. For n ≥ 3, Mathlib's cycleGraph_isContained_iff identifies an IsCycle walk of length n with a not-necessarily-induced copy of C_n. Reparametrizing odd lengths as 2*k+1 and shifting an existential threshold preserves eventual containment. The full formulation equivalence and the strict/non-strict threshold equivalence were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the problem's sorry-backed theorems.

reformulations.difference: Replaces χ(G) ≥ ℵ₂ by nonexistence of a proper colouring into every type α with #α ≤ ℵ₁.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The hypothesis says precisely that every proper colouring requires more than ℵ₁ colours. Since ℵ₂ is the successor cardinal of ℵ₁, this is equivalent to χ(G) ≥ ℵ₂. The full equivalence, including the cycle-containment conclusion, was proved as Review594.historical_formulation_iff in the scratch file using only standard axioms.

Erdős, Problems and results in chromatic graph theory (1969), p. 31: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1969-13.pdf
Erdős, Hajnal, and Shelah, On some general properties of chromatic numbers (1974), §4, Theorem 3 and the preceding historical remark, pp. 250–251: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1974-17.pdf

review.notes: All three declarations were checked. The positive answer and solved categories agree with the cited original literature. The exact linked external Lean proof compiled successfully, and #print axioms reported only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Boundary checks covered empty/countable vertex types, complete graphs witnessing both cardinal hypotheses, the distinction between ℵ₁ and ℵ₂, the excluded length-one cycle, and small genuine/repeated walks. The sanity-check theorem also has only standard axioms. Direct access to erdosproblems.com/594 was blocked by a Cloudflare challenge despite descriptive User-Agent headers; the mathematical review therefore relied on the cited primary papers. The reviewed repository file was not modified.
